Abel also said there is a lot more pushback in communities across the US on new data center construction, and that a data center has to be a welcomed member of the community.

original.text:
US gas prices are climbing, and it is not because the world ran out of crude.

The Strait of Hormuz has been shut or contested since March. Gulf producers are not refusing to sell, they simply cannot ship. Diesel leaving the Gulf has fallen from roughly 800,000 barrels a day to 165,000.

Europe lost that supply and started bidding for Atlantic cargoes instead. So American refiners are now exporting a record 1.9 million barrels a day of distillate, mostly to north-west Europe, and US stocks drain to cover it.

The binding constraint is refining, not crude (yet). US capacity is 18.2 million barrels a day, down from 19.0 in 2020.

Gasoline is 205.7 million, nine below the bottom of that range, and has been under it for 17 straight weeks. Distillate is 104.2 million, the lowest reading for this week in 44 years of records.

The barrels are there. The fuel is thinning. But barrel are there, because they can't be processed.

That is what pushes the number on the pump.

Take one gallon apart. In the week to 24 August, regular gasoline cost $4.08: $2.01 of crude, $1.55 of refining, $0.52 of distribution and tax. Diesel cost $5.65 from the same $2.01 of crude, plus $2.26 of refining.

Same barrel, same crude slice. What differs is the refining margin, and that is the part that exploded. Diesel's is 46% wider than gasoline's, $95 a barrel against $65.

text:
US gas prices are climbing, and it is not because the world ran out of crude.

The Strait of Hormuz has been shut or contested since March. Gulf producers are not refusing to sell, they simply cannot ship. Diesel leaving the Gulf has fallen from roughly 800,000 barrels a day to 165,000.

Europe lost that supply and started bidding for Atlantic cargoes instead. So American refiners are now exporting a record 1.9 million barrels a day of distillate, mostly to north-west Europe, and US stocks drain to cover it.

The binding constraint is refining, not crude (yet). US capacity is 18.2 million barrels a day, down from 19.0 in 2020.

PLAN FOR THIS WEEK:

Last week I marked 767 as the line in the sand. Friday’s upside retest failed. The session closed as a daily inside bar / bearish Harami — a red compression candle fully contained inside Thursday’s range. That pattern does not resolve quietly.

The 766 gap is now the level that matters. The 50-day sits directly beneath it. That is confluence, not coincidence. A retest of that shelf is the base case.

GEX agrees with the chart: • Flip / vol trigger: 771 • Put wall: 770 • Call wall: 773 • Largest positive gamma: 775 • Negative gamma stacked 760–768

Only bullish regime is a reclaim and hold of 771. Everything under that points to filling 766, then the 750 gap — where flow has been accumulating — into the 748–740 Fib golden zone. 

That pocket is still a higher-low inside the rising channel. Lose 740 and the structure argument is dead.

Week: PPI Thursday, CPI Friday, FOMC Sep 15–16. Fed is in the quiet period. Waller: hold if August inflation keeps cooling, hike if it comes in hot. 

Iran/Hormuz flared again over the weekend. Oil is the wild card into the print.

Play the levels. 767 lost = do not catch the knife. 771 reclaimed = dealers start damping again.
NFA. #SPY #GEX #CPI #FOMC #OptionsFlow

$SPY 

Everyone’s getting caught up in these massive swings, comparing it to last year… when in reality this is starting to look a lot more like 2022.

Back then we’d rip 8% in a few days just to dump even harder right after. We’re not at that magnitude yet but that’s exactly how it starts.

These violent moves aren’t random. Their purpose is to trap you get you buying too early or shorting too early so by the time the market is actually down 20–30%, your capital is already tied up.

That’s how most people miss the real opportunity.

I’d rather stay patient, wait for the real washout, and go heavy near the bottom. Then on the first higher low confirmation, that’s when you press.

Because when this cycle resets and rates eventually come down, the next leg up won’t be small. It will be like 2021 UP ONLY.

Distributions made by the Funds have been classified as a return of capital and may be comprised of option premiums, dividends, capital gains, and interest payments. Please see the 19a-1 notices for an estimated breakdown of monthly distributions on each Fund's page. Distributions are not guaranteed.

*The Advisor has contractually agreed to keep the net expenses of IWMI from exceeding 0.68% of the Fund's average daily net assets through September 30, 2026 and the net expenses of NIHI from exceeding 0.68% of the Fund's average daily net assets through September 10, 2026 subject to approval of the agreement by the Board. Without the fee waiver IWMI’s expenses would be 0.76% and NIHI’s expenses would be 0.75%.  BTCI’s total annual fund operating expenses are 0.99%.

**30-day SEC Yield is calculation based on a formula mandated by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) that calculates a fund's hypothetical annualized income, as a percentage of its assets. A security's income, for the purposes of this calculation, is based on the current market yield to maturity (in the case of bonds) or projected dividend yield (for stocks) of the fund's holdings over a trailing 30-day period. This hypothetical income will differ (at times, significantly) from the fund's actual experience; as a result, income distributions from the fund may be higher or lower than implied by the SEC yield. It is important to note that 30-Day SEC Yield does not include income received from option selling. The data reflects the most recent month-end (5/31/2026). The Unsubsidized 30-day SEC Yield represents what a fund’s 30-day SEC yield would be had no fee waiver been in place over the reporting period. IWMI = 0.46% and NIHI = 2.64%.

Distribution Rate: The annualized rate an investor would receive if the Fund’s most recent distribution remained constant. It reflects a single distribution, not the Fund’s total return, and is calculated by annualizing the most recent distribution (multiplying by 12) and dividing by the Fund’s most recent ex-date NAV.

first — not every stock is going to be a winner. that's the whole point of stop losses. know where you're wrong before you enter, and get out when the train derails. no exceptions.

$SNOW $CRWD $NET $SHOP $MSFT $TEAM $NOW $CRM $MDB $OSCR $UNH .......

but soon — i think we're setting up for the kind of run that makes generational wealth. not this week. not next week. but the setup is loading.

next theme i'm watching — staples, uranium and metals. i'll post more when the charts confirm.

original.text:
$SPY $SPX 

PLAN FOR THIS WEEK:

Last week I marked 767 as the line in the sand. Friday’s upside retest failed. The session closed as a daily inside bar / bearish Harami — a red compression candle fully contained inside Thursday’s range. That pattern does not resolve quietly.

The 766 gap is now the level that matters. The 50-day sits directly beneath it. That is confluence, not coincidence. A retest of that shelf is the base case.

GEX agrees with the chart: • Flip / vol trigger: 771 • Put wall: 770 • Call wall: 773 • Largest positive gamma: 775 • Negative gamma stacked 760–768

Only bullish regime is a reclaim and hold of 771. Everything under that points to filling 766, then the 750 gap — where flow has been accumulating — into the 748–740 Fib golden zone. 

That pocket is still a higher-low inside the rising channel. Lose 740 and the structure argument is dead.

Week: PPI Thursday, CPI Friday, FOMC Sep 15–16. Fed is in the quiet period. Waller: hold if August inflation keeps cooling, hike if it comes in hot. 

Iran/Hormuz flared again over the weekend. Oil is the wild card into the print.

Play the levels. 767 lost = do not catch the knife. 771 reclaimed = dealers start damping again.
NFA. #SPY #GEX #CPI #FOMC #OptionsFlow

Supply disruptions don’t magically disappear because someone says they will.

Those barrels don’t magically reappear. Tankers don’t magically repair themselves. Shipping companies don’t ignore the risk. Insurance doesn’t get cheaper while vessels are being attacked.

Every additional disruption has the potential to tighten physical supply and make moving the remaining barrels more expensive.

And the effects don’t necessarily show up at the gas pump immediately. They work their way through the system.

That’s the part people are missing.

text:
The S&P 500 had its chance to change structure last week… and FAILED. 

Instead of clearing the August 28th high, price pushed back into that Golden Pocket and rejected it for the second time.

Personally, I do NOT think we clear that August 28th high before going lower.

And now my weekly signal line has officially closed RED for only the third time this year.

The previous two?

The signal flipped red earlier this year before the roughly 10% March decline.

It flipped red again in June before the roughly 5% decline.

Now it’s red again.

That does NOT mean we automatically get another 5-10% selloff. But when I combine my signals with market structure, crude oil, VIX, yields, geopolitical risk and midterm seasonality, I continue to see a minimum 3% pullback as the highest probability path.

And I want to emphasize the word MINIMUM.

Could it turn into 4%? 5%? More? Absolutely.

But here’s something people seem to forget. 

A 3-5% pullback does NOT kill a bull market.

We can absolutely get the pullback I’m looking for and still turn around and make new all time highs before the end of the year.

Pullbacks happen in bullish regimes.

They’re normal.

I’m not calling for the end of the bull market.

I’m calling for a pullback BEFORE I start looking for the next leg higher unless monthly signals go bearish after this next pullback. 

For now, structure remains structure.

And until price proves otherwise, I’m following it.

— TJ

text:
The market is a game of probabilities.

Everything we do as traders is built around probabilities and risk management.

Whether you’re looking at gamma charts that have worked in the past, heat maps with key nodes that repeatedly attract price, mathematically based indicators, support and resistance, liquidity, volume or market structure…

NONE of it predicts the future with certainty.

It simply helps us determine what is more likely to happen based on the information we have.

A gamma level can work 10 times and fail the 11th. A Golden Node can attract price over and over and then get completely ignored. An indicator can have an incredible historical track record and still lose on the very next trade.

That doesn’t mean the tool stopped working.

It means probabilities are not guarantees.

That’s why risk management matters just as much as the setup itself.

You don’t need to know exactly what the market is going to do next. You need a thesis with favorable probabilities, a defined level where you’re wrong, and position sizing that allows you to survive when the probability doesn’t play out.

I don’t trade certainty.

I trade probabilities.

And when I’m wrong? I take the loss and move on to the next setup.

That’s the game.

text:
THREE Iranian oil tankers were just struck by the United States TODAY.

And people still don’t understand why I have $120+ Crude Oil on my radar. 👀

WTI finished Friday around $91/barrel.

My target remains $120+ within the next 2 months.

But here’s what I think people are missing. 

The oil shock is already underway but the FULL effects haven’t worked their way through the system yet.

We’ve already had major disruption through the Strait of Hormuz. Tankers carrying Saudi crude were attacked this week. Now Iranian oil tankers have been struck.

And every additional tanker damaged, shipping route disrupted, barrel taken offline, insurance premium increased or company unwilling to risk sending ships through the region puts additional pressure on the physical oil market.

But that doesn’t mean you see the entire impact at the gas pump tomorrow.

There’s a lag.

Crude reprices first. Then those costs work through refiners, wholesale gasoline, inventories, transportation and distribution before ultimately reaching consumers.

Historically, EIA research has found roughly half of a crude price change can reach retail gasoline within about two weeks and roughly 80% within four weeks, all else equal.

And then there’s the political wildcard.

The Trump administration has an obvious incentive to de escalate before the midterms. Higher crude and gasoline create another inflation and cost of living problem heading into November.

But peace isn’t solely Washington’s decision.

Iran has its own incentives and objectives.

Could Tehran recognize that continued escalation, disruption through Hormuz and higher oil prices would create additional political pressure on Trump and Republicans heading into the midterms? Absolutely.

But I’m not going to claim that proves Iran’s strategy is specifically to send crude to $120 or determine the U.S. election. We simply don’t know that.

What we DO know is that continued escalation creates exactly the type of environment where another supply shock can develop.

More tanker attacks. More retaliation. More shipping disruptions. More barrels potentially taken offline.

And if the physical supply situation deteriorates further?

That’s where I believe crude can get violent.

My thesis remains:

$120 Crude Oil within the next 2 months.

And if that happens, this becomes much bigger than oil.

Higher energy costs can feed inflation, squeeze consumers, complicate the Fed’s job, pressure Treasury yields and create another problem for equities.

The oil shock isn’t something I’m waiting to START.

I’m waiting for what has already started to work its way through the system.

Things are heating up…

$SPX $SPY #SP500 $ES_F $QQQ $NDX $CL_F #US10Y $TLT #CrudeOil #Oil

— TJ

LATE NIGHT CHECK. 🌙

When you think you have it bad, just remember… somebody out there has it much worse.

We spend so much time stressing about what went wrong, what we don’t have, how far behind we are or what could happen tomorrow that sometimes we forget how damn lucky we are just to have another day to try.

Jim Rohn once said:

“If you think trying is risky, wait till they hand you the bill for not trying.”

That one has always stuck with me.

Take the risk. Chase the goal. Tell your people you love them. Stop waiting for the “perfect” time to start living the life you actually want.

You’re going to have bad days. You’re going to lose. You’re going to get knocked on your ass.

But somebody would give EVERYTHING to have the problems you’re complaining about tonight.

Be grateful. Keep going. And give it another shot tomorrow.

Goodnight everyone!

— TJ

We believe the response to this question deserves a post:

We think the biggest gap was underestimating how durable $LULU product and brand moat would be in North America. We initially viewed the issues more as cyclical, but competition and weaker product innovation proved more structural than we expected. Also the high ROIC and strong China growth gave us confidence that the business remained strong.

That said, we were trimming throughout as the thesis weakened, 1% in Q1 2025 and then exited in Q3, when the position was down to 1.95% of our total portfolio.

In hindsight, we should have put more weight on the possibility that the moat itself was weakening, rather than assuming the business would eventually recover to its previous trajectory.

text:
Is the market truly rational, or does it just outsource valuation?

Yesterday, $PYPL was trading at $61.47. Today, it’s down ~16% in pre-market ($51.67) on reports that the Advent & Stripe consortium abandoned their $50B+ acquisition pursuit.

Think about the psychological aspect here:

The market immediately erased the majority of the buyout premium because a potential buyer walked away.

But Negotiation ≠ Intrinsic Value: A competitor/PE firm walking away doesn’t mean the business suddenly lost 16% of its underlying cash-generating capacity overnight. 

It simply means the buyer wasn't willing to meet PayPal's higher asking price at this stage, or capital allocation priorities shifted.

Yesterday’s price reflected takeover speculation; today’s price reflects rejection shock but neither necessarily reflects fundamental intrinsic value.

When a bidder steps back from the table, are they proving the company is worth less?

What’s your take: Is this an overreaction and buying opportunity, or is the market right to re-rate $PYPL lower without M&A support?

text:
The $UBER vs $TSLA debate happening right now across the board is fascinating in many respects.

I’ve spent all day reading both sides. I even went to ChatGPT and had a conversation with Astra because of how fascinating this debate is to me. 

By the way, Astra is legit. Releasing that before Anthropic’s IPO was a chess move. The frontier lab wars are only getting more intense. 

I am long both in small quantities. A bit of Tesla I bought a year ago at $350 and haven’t added since and a small amount of Uber I added 2 weeks ago at $75 after taking a look at the numbers. Not short any of the names but also not meaningfully long any of them at this moment either. 

My conclusion so far is both sides are being ridiculously extreme in their conclusion. 

The extreme $UBER bulls are not seriously acknowledging the direct existisitential threat to its moat via CyberCab’s pure product experience and eventual scale.

The extreme $TSLA bulls are not giving any merit to the 200M+ monthly users they have, how hard is it to scale a network, how self driving might be commoditized and Uber could simply become the largest marketplace for multiple vendors, and how much time unsupervised true autonomy will take to reach any meaningful level of Uber’s 42M daily rides.

Honestly, I think both will do well. I don’t think it has to be as black or white as both sides are making it. 

However, it is an incredible thought experiment. Uber disrupted transportation forever with technology, and now Tesla is disrupting transportation forever with autonomy. 

I think Uber is undervalued. I think Tesla has the most exciting potential out of all the Mag 7 over the next decade.

I just think both sides are writing off the other for no reason.

The funniest outcome would be an eventual partnership even though I know it’s not that likely, but I do think this is going to not be one or the other.

original.text:
The market is being very stupid about Reddit's Q2 report, after its weakness in US DAUq combined with comments about 'choppy' search referral traffic. $RDDT 

This rising era of "Google Zero" (zero click-through) from AI search summaries has the market way too skittish here.

Yes, US DAUq (daily uniques) retreated -300K sequentially. It means users that were using the site/app daily didn't engage every single day in the middle of summer. Those users are now likely in US WAUq (weekly uniques), which grew +700K. 

The market is forgetting that net new DAUq in Q2 is always seasonally weak. A sequential pullback like this has happened 6 times in 6 years, half of which were in a Q2. 

What I think is vastly more important as a gauge of Reddit's ongoing executional success is their +64% ad revenue growth. This primarily comes from higher user engagement (more opportunities for ad impressions) and a rise in ad pricing from improved ad performance and/or higher demand. (Another lever they have is the number of ad impressions over a piece of content, which they thankfully pull infrequently. The COO says so when they do, and she did not mention it.)

If you invest in $RDDT you need to downplay the importance of DAUq/WAUq in your quarterly measures of executional success. These user-focused KPIs mask the fact that mgmt isn't giving you enough info to gauge user engagement & ad impressions on your own. So you have to trust the revenue numbers and ARPU (rev per DAUq) being generated as your primary view.

DAUq/WAUq KPIs only tell you frequency of visits. It tells you nothing about the amount of user engagement per visit and from that, the number of ad impressions served to the user over that time.

As a rough example of why the underlying user engagement is the key factor (which DAUq is a secondary input into), a daily user might be coming to the site for 5 minutes per day (35min a week).  Another weekly user might be coming to the site two days a week for an hour each (120min a week). These 2 users end up with wildly different engagement times that are completely masked by these "critical" KPIs.  In my example, that weekly user is driving over 3x the enagement of that daily.

We also have no idea what each user is doing in that time per visit: are they reading long threads in the comments? visiting multiple posts in rapid fire without diving in depth into comments? moderating a subreddit? scrolling a feed? using DMs? or watching linked videos on a single page?  A user watching linked videos are not generating anywhere near the same amount of ad impressions than a user reading deep into the comments across multiple posts.

So the real levers for Reddit operationally are in how many ad impressions and what types of ads and content (posts, comments, feeds, searchs) they are exposed to during that each visit, and ultimately, the performance of their ad engine in matching these ads to high-intent users.  

ARPU rose +51% in the US despite the sequential drop in DAUq. That tells us that Reddit is successfully improving ad monetization through higher engagement and improved ad performance leading to higher pricing/demand.

The 'choppy' click-through from AI search summaries are giving everyone across the open web some slight to severe weakness in referrals. Reddit has several paths forward should it worsen (including its still ongoing data licensing renegotiation with Google). But all of the signs within revenue/ARPU are pointing to continued strong execution by the Reddit team over the levers they can control.

Podcast: Trasteel CEO Gianfranco Imperato on Trade Disruption and a Changing Steel Market (SZZL)

This week, we speak with Gianfranco Imperato, CEO of Trasteel, and Jamie Karson, Vice Chairman of Sizzle Acquisition Corp. II $SZZL . The two announced a $1.3bn deal in April.

It has been an interesting year for steel as it has been the target of trade restrictions and supply chain snares. In the center of that all has been steel producing and trading platform Trasteel.

Gianfranco explains how the company has been an active consolidator in the industry that has managed to avoid certain operational risks despite an ever-changing steel pricing situation. He also gets into how the company has been able to leverage its global platform to be opportunistic when trade disruptions shake up the market.

Jamie tells us why Sizzle II admired Trasteel’s financial discipline and why it sees the company’s business as being upstream of some of the world’s biggest investment trends of the moment.

Give it a listen.

https://t.co/9XO1Zde5GQ

PODCAST: ZincFive and Spark I Acquisition Corp $SPKL 

We spoke with Tod Higinbotham, CEO of battery maker @zincfiveinc and Jim Rhee, Chairman and CEO of Spark I Acquisition Corp. $SPKL . The two announced a $752M deal in June.

Lithium-ion batteries have dominated much of the conversation in cutting-edge technology. But, what if there was a battery chemistry based on more available materials that were more recyclable and that were an even better fit for certain data center energy needs?

Tod explains how ZincFive’s nickel and zinc-based battery chemistry is uniquely suited to providing high-density backup power to data centers, and how this SPAC transaction will help it meet the ballooning demand for its products.

Jim also gets into how the company’s unique financial profile in the battery space made it a particularly interesting target, and how the SPAC’s management team plans to help ZincFive expand into new markets.

Give it a listen.

Cantor Equity Partners I $CEPO terminates its crypto treasury deal with BSTR. 

CEPO gets a $15M termination fee, but they only have less than 5 months left on their clock to find a new target company. Deadline is currently early Jan 2027. 

Plus, the Cantor Equity Partners team already has four other SPACs out searching with significantly more time left making those terms more attractive to potential targets compared to CEPO.

As a result, there's a possibility CEPO liquidates (like Churchill IX). Keep in mind that if CEPO eventually does liquidate, the sponsor already stated they would contribute $0.15 per share to redemption events on top of what is already held in trust. Part of that $15M termination fee would probably help pay for that.

Podcast: AIR CEO Stuart Brazier on AIR’s $1.7B SPAC Deal and the Business of Hookah ( $CAEP )

This week, we speak with Stuart Brazier, CEO of Advanced Inhalation Rituals, or AIR, to discuss his company’s $1.7 billion combination with Cantor Equity Partners III (Nasdaq: CAEP).

SPACs often bring companies from emerging technology sectors into the public markets, but sometimes it is their role to list companies that have already established themselves, albeit in something of a niche.

Podcast: Inside Key Mining’s $303M Deal with Compass Digital Acquisition Corp. $CDAQF

We spoke with @keyminingcorp founders Cesar Lopez and John Ryan as well as Compass Digital Acquisition Corp. CEO Tom Hennessy to break down their $303M business combination.

Titanium, copper and water. What do they have in common? All will be products of one of the latest companies to head to the public markets via a SPAC transaction.

Cesar and John discuss how they brought together a signature titanium mining project in Chile with a water desalination project that is set to support it. They lay out why they are combining these two assets with a copper project in Arizona and how both stand to benefit from the critical metals incentives in the Inflation Reduction Act.

Tom explains how this company fits in his growing family of SPAC transactions and what the roadmap ahead looks like for it beyond close and the listing this deal brings.

Give it a listen.

AlphaTarget is now more than two years old, and I’ve been reflecting on what we’ve learned.

We’ve beaten the S&P 500 by a wide margin. I’m proud of that but what matters even more to us is how we build on it from here.

The last two years have been an extraordinary period for AI and technology and they’ve taught us a great deal about both opportunity and risk.

We’ve now become much more deliberate about portfolio construction and risk management. We still want to own the companies with the potential to reshape industries and compound capital for years but we also recognise that growth stocks have become super volatile and periods of extreme optimism are inevitably followed by sharp resets.

That means more active portfolio management, taking gains when appropriate, genuine hedging when conditions warrant it and holding more cash when markets become excessively extended.

We refined our portfolio management and hedging strategy this spring, and June and July provided the first serious test.

During those two months, many AI stocks fell 40–60%. AlphaTarget’s portfolio declined roughly 20%.

It was still a testing period but the portfolio held up considerably better than it had during previous periods of market volatility.

We don’t view that as the end of the story, it’s the beginning of a better process.

Our objective for the next several years is straightforward:

Find exceptional companies early. Participate aggressively when the opportunity is greatest and manage the portfolio actively to reduce drawdowns when the market inevitably becomes volatile.

The opportunity created by AI and the technologies surrounding it remains enormous.

At the same time, the longer this bull market runs, the greater the risk that parts of the market become speculative (real risk of an AI bubble in the future). I believe navigating that environment - knowing when to be aggressive and when to protect capital - will be one of the defining investment challenges over the next 2-3 years.

And frankly, I think the next 2-3 years could be even more interesting than the last two.

To all our subscribers, thank you for being on this journey with us.

If you’re discovering AlphaTarget for the first time, our research service provides institutional-quality research on the most promising companies in the public markets, along with timely Trading Alerts so subscribers can follow our portfolio decisions as they happen. https://t.co/YKr5pL7G2c

text:
The launch of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra marks a clear transition in AI capabilities: moving from copilot assistance (generating text and code) towards direct computer control (executing multi-step workflows across applications, terminals, and browsers).  

While the technical jump is substantial, deployment remains gated under enterprise admin controls and access restrictions; meaning adoption will be measured, not overnight.  

Investment Implications: 

Legacy SaaS (Value Compression): Seat-based SaaS pricing faces structural pressure as agents execute workflows that previously required individual user seats. Mid-tier apps acting primarily as thin GUIs risk being reduced to low-margin systems of record.  

Inference & Power (Structural Demand): Multi-step, agentic execution increases token volume and compute per completed job relative to single-prompt queries. This sustains high capital intensity across compute, networking and energy infrastructure.  

Context & Governance Holders (Durable Moats): Models require live operational context to act safely. Value and pricing power accrue to platforms that control proprietary enterprise data, identity, permissions and audit logs.  

Bottom Line: Value is likely to shift away from thin middle-layer application software, concentrating instead in underlying compute and power infrastructure and in the platform layers governing enterprise execution.

text:
When I was younger, probably like 5th or 6th grade, I was doing the annoying thing of repeatedly asking the same question, specifically the inquiry if my dad was willing to live somewhere?

“Would you live in Arizona?”

“Would you live in Wyoming?”

Eventually, maybe 9 or 10 states in, I got to Connecticut. 

My dad turns to me and says “Son, I’d live anywhere for the right number. There’s always a number.”

And that has stuck with me for roughly 3 decades.

text:
Weekly Tesla Update

TESLA PUTS DRIVERLESS CYBERCABS ON AUSTIN STREETS, AND SAFETY REGULATORS ARE ALREADY WATCHING
$TSLA began offering public rides in its two seat Cybercab in limited parts of Austin, Texas, a vehicle built with no steering wheel and no pedals, and NHTSA said it is in contact with the company and evaluating the situation. Elon Musk skipped the launch event, where executives spent roughly 15 minutes on pricing, manufacturing and technology while floating dynamic pricing at what they billed as coach prices. State records show $TSLA had 420 autonomous vehicles registered in Texas, including 45 Cybercabs, versus 988 for $GOOGL unit Waymo, the current U.S. leader.

TESLA EUROPE NUMBERS SPLIT WIDE OPEN IN AUGUST
$TSLA registrations across Europe were mixed in August, with sharp gains in France and Denmark offset by steep declines in Norway and Sweden. European sales have rebounded this year after two consecutive annual declines, aided by easier comparisons, higher fuel prices, government incentives and rising interest in electric vehicles. Data from Britain and Germany, the region's two largest markets, is due later this week.

TESLA CLAIMS 1 MILLION UNSUPERVISED ROBOTAXI MILES, WITH MOST OF IT LOGGED IN THE LAST SIX WEEKS
$TSLA said its Robotaxi fleet has now driven 1 million miles without a human supervising, up from 380,000 miles disclosed on the Q2 earnings call in July. AI chief Ashok Elluswamy announced the milestone at the Austin Cybercab event, marking roughly 620,000 added unsupervised miles in about six weeks. The jump reflects a shift in mix as much as growth, since $TSLA only began running unsupervised miles at the start of this year and paid ridership was flat last quarter at roughly 900,000 added miles.

TESLA CLAIMS 1 MILLION UNSUPERVISED ROBOTAXI MILES, WITH MOST OF IT LOGGED IN THE LAST SIX WEEKS
$TSLA said its Robotaxi fleet has now driven 1 million miles without a human supervising, up from 380,000 miles disclosed on the Q2 earnings call in July. AI chief Ashok Elluswamy announced the milestone at the Austin Cybercab event, marking roughly 620,000 added unsupervised miles in about six weeks. The jump reflects a shift in mix as much as growth, since $TSLA only began running unsupervised miles at the start of this year and paid ridership was flat last quarter at roughly 900,000 added miles.

Weekly NVIDIA Update

AMAZON AND NVIDIA GO ALL IN: 2 MILLION MORE GPUS AND AI FACTORIES FOR WASHINGTON
AWS and $NVDA are expanding their 16 year partnership to deploy 2 million additional Blackwell Ultra, Rubin and Rubin Ultra GPUs across AWS global infrastructure in 2027 and 2028, well above the 1 million $AMZN flagged at GTC earlier this year. The deal also brings $NVDA Vera CPUs to AWS, extends NVLink Fusion with custom NVHBM memory into Annapurna Labs Trainium chips, and includes AI factories for the US government with 100,000 GPUs on secure infrastructure cleared for Impact Level 6 workloads and above. Rounding it out: Nemotron open models on Bedrock and SageMaker, GPU accelerated data processing on EMR, and Amazon Robotics adopting the $NVDA physical AI stack for warehouse automation.

NVIDIA DROPS $3.5 BILLION ON MEDIATEK TO LOCK DOWN THE AI STACK
$NVDA is investing $3.5 billion in Taiwan's MediaTek via bonds convertible into MediaTek shares, deepening a partnership that will see the chipmaker adopt NVLink Fusion and the newly announced NVHBM technology. The deal keeps $NVDA at the center of the data center hardware chain even as customers design their own accelerators, and it lands just after $AMZN pledged to deploy 2 million more Nvidia components alongside its own silicon.

text:
Weekly Tesla Update

TESLA RECALLS 3 MILLION VEHICLES IN CHINA OVER DOOR HANDLES AND DRIVER MONITORING
$TSLA is voluntarily recalling about 3 million vehicles in China after warning that severe collisions can knock out the low voltage system and leave its retractable door handles inoperable, trapping occupants inside and impeding rescuers. A second recall addresses deficient driver attention monitoring, with $TSLA adding in cabin camera monitoring alongside steering wheel torque sensors via free software updates. Eight other automakers issued their own door handle recalls the same day as Chinese regulators tighten rules on the flush design $TSLA popularized, with U.S. regulators now weighing a similar mandate.

TESLA SETS CYBERCAB LAUNCH FOR SEPTEMBER 3, BUT THE FLEET BEHIND IT IS STILL TINY
$TSLA will debut its two seat, steering wheel free Cybercab at an invite only Austin event on September 3, opening it to hails through the existing Robotaxi app for top scorers in its rider sweepstakes, with a livestream for everyone else. The car is new but the software is not, running the same FSD stack that powers the Model Y robotaxis, and independent trackers still put $TSLA's active unsupervised fleet at roughly 20 to 30 vehicles against Waymo's 3,000 plus and 500,000 weekly paid trips. The Cybercab's main edge is efficiency at about 165 Wh per mile versus 250 to 280 for a Model Y, a modest unit economics win that comes with three fewer seats and almost no room for luggage, strollers, or wheelchairs.

TESLA KILLS SOLAR ROOF AND REBUILDS ITS SOLAR BUSINESS AROUND PANELS AND POWERWALL
$TSLA discontinued the glass Solar Roof it launched in 2016, a product that reached only about 3,000 US installs by the end of 2022, and is now centering the business on a new US made 420 watt panel built in Buffalo and bundled by default with Powerwall 3.

Weekly AI Update

OPENAI'S FIRST CHIP TAKES AIM AT NVIDIA'S MOST PROFITABLE TURF
OpenAI unveiled Jalapeño, an inference chip built with $AVGO that it says beat $NVDA's Blackwell systems on performance per watt in nearly all tested scenarios, with deployment inside OpenAI's own compute infrastructure expected by year end. 

AMAZON TRIPLES ITS NVIDIA CHIP ORDER JUST FIVE MONTHS AFTER THE LAST ONE
$AMZN is adding another 2 million $NVDA GPUs to AWS data centers across 2027 and 2028, including Blackwell Ultra, Rubin and Rubin Ultra, a deal worth tens of billions of dollars that comes only five months after a commitment of more than 1 million chips. The expanded partnership also pulls $NVDA networking, CPUs, open models and its robotics stack into AWS, even as $AMZN pushes its own competing Trainium and Graviton silicon, now at a $25 billion annualized run rate.

APPLE GOES 2 NM WITH M6 AND BUILDS ITS BIGGEST CHIP EVER
$AAPL debuted the M6 in a new Mac mini and the M5 Ultra in a new Mac Studio, with M6 becoming the company's first 2 nanometer chip, packing a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine that doubles peak AI compute versus the prior generation. The M5 Ultra is $AAPL's most powerful chip to date, using UltraFusion to link four dies for the first time, with up to a 36-core CPU, an 80-core GPU, 512GB of unified memory and 1.2TB/s of bandwidth, 50 percent more than M3 Ultra. Both are aimed squarely at running large AI models locally on device rather than in the cloud.

Set a new all-time high in the only P&L that really matters: being the best father I could be and dadmaxxing all summer long.

My kids are still in that fleeting little window where they want Dad right there beside them for everything, and every day the reality sinks in a little deeper that no amount of money I make in the market will ever be enough to buy these moments back.

Packed in as many core memories for them as I possibly could, hoping that one day, when they have families of their own, they’ll look back on these years as the blueprint for what it means to be an awesome dad.

The bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki killed 150,000 to 246,000 people.

original.text:
US gas prices are climbing, and it is not because the world ran out of crude.

The Strait of Hormuz has been shut or contested since March. Gulf producers are not refusing to sell, they simply cannot ship. Diesel leaving the Gulf has fallen from roughly 800,000 barrels a day to 165,000.

Europe lost that supply and started bidding for Atlantic cargoes instead. So American refiners are now exporting a record 1.9 million barrels a day of distillate, mostly to north-west Europe, and US stocks drain to cover it.

The binding constraint is refining, not crude (yet). US capacity is 18.2 million barrels a day, down from 19.0 in 2020.

None of this means Hormuz has stopped mattering. We are in the first phase of the shock, and it shows up in inventories rather than in the crude price.

Look at what is actually short. US crude stocks excluding the SPR sit at 424.5 million barrels, comfortably inside their five-year range for the week. Gasoline is 205.7 million, nine below the bottom of that range, and has been under it for 17 straight weeks. Distillate is 104.2 million, the lowest reading for this week in 44 years of records.

The barrels are there. The fuel is thinning. But barrel are there, because they can't be processed.

That is what pushes the number on the pump.

Take one gallon apart. In the week to 24 August, regular gasoline cost $4.08: $2.01 of crude, $1.55 of refining, $0.52 of distribution and tax. Diesel cost $5.65 from the same $2.01 of crude, plus $2.26 of refining.

Same barrel, same crude slice. What differs is the refining margin, and that is the part that exploded. Diesel's is 46% wider than gasoline's, $95 a barrel against $65.

Podcast: Trasteel CEO Gianfranco Imperato on Trade Disruption and a Changing Steel Market (SZZL)

This week, we speak with Gianfranco Imperato, CEO of Trasteel, and Jamie Karson, Vice Chairman of Sizzle Acquisition Corp. II $SZZL . The two announced a $1.3bn deal in April.

It has been an interesting year for steel as it has been the target of trade restrictions and supply chain snares. In the center of that all has been steel producing and trading platform Trasteel.

Gianfranco explains how the company has been an active consolidator in the industry that has managed to avoid certain operational risks despite an ever-changing steel pricing situation. He also gets into how the company has been able to leverage its global platform to be opportunistic when trade disruptions shake up the market.

Jamie tells us why Sizzle II admired Trasteel’s financial discipline and why it sees the company’s business as being upstream of some of the world’s biggest investment trends of the moment.

Give it a listen.

https://t.co/9XO1Zde5GQ

PODCAST: ZincFive and Spark I Acquisition Corp $SPKL 

We spoke with Tod Higinbotham, CEO of battery maker @zincfiveinc and Jim Rhee, Chairman and CEO of Spark I Acquisition Corp. $SPKL . The two announced a $752M deal in June.

Lithium-ion batteries have dominated much of the conversation in cutting-edge technology. But, what if there was a battery chemistry based on more available materials that were more recyclable and that were an even better fit for certain data center energy needs?

Tod explains how ZincFive’s nickel and zinc-based battery chemistry is uniquely suited to providing high-density backup power to data centers, and how this SPAC transaction will help it meet the ballooning demand for its products.

Jim also gets into how the company’s unique financial profile in the battery space made it a particularly interesting target, and how the SPAC’s management team plans to help ZincFive expand into new markets.

Give it a listen.

https://t.co/EvXCrJywBw

PODCAST: Dr. Wasiq Bokhari, CEO of Quantum Computing Firm Pasqal $BBCQ 

This week, we speak with Dr. Wasiq Bokhari, CEO of quantum computing firm Pasqal, to discuss its $1.98 billion combination with Bleichroeder Acquisition Corp. II $BBCQ .

Quantum computers are plugged in and doing real commercial work, but, how can you get them to collaborate with CPUs and GPUs on a single problem? @pasqal_quantum believes it may have the answer.

Wasiq explains how the company has worked to build a full-stack approach to commercializing quantum solutions and where it has already demonstrated quantum advantage.

He also gets into how it is developing software to make engaging with quantum computers easier, and how it can break down problems into the parts that quantum computers, CPUs and GPUs are each best poised to solve the fastest.

Podcast: AIR CEO Stuart Brazier on AIR’s $1.7B SPAC Deal and the Business of Hookah ( $CAEP )

This week, we speak with Stuart Brazier, CEO of Advanced Inhalation Rituals, or AIR, to discuss his company’s $1.7 billion combination with Cantor Equity Partners III (Nasdaq: CAEP).

SPACs often bring companies from emerging technology sectors into the public markets, but sometimes it is their role to list companies that have already established themselves, albeit in something of a niche.

Stuart explains how the AIR’s profitable position in the high-margin hookah-shisha market gave it options on how to come public, and why it chose the SPAC route for that journey. How is this lifestyle brand growing and where? And, what additional revenue streams are there still to be had from its 600-year-old core product?

Podcast: General Fusion’s Greg Twinney & Spring Valley III’s Chris Sorrells $SVAC 

On this week’s podcast, we speak with Greg Twinney, CEO of @GeneralFusion , and Chris Sorrells, CEO and Chairman of Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III (NASDAQ:SVAC). The two announced a $724M deal in January.

Fusion technology may sound like the future, but it is set to come to the public markets very soon. Greg explains General Fusion’s path to expand its technology beyond its first plant into commercialization in the 2030s, and what advantages fusion power plants can provide over nuclear fission reactors.

Chris lays out why now is the right time to bring General Fusion to the public markets, and how the Spring Valley team put a price on the opportunity at this stage in its development.

Give it a listen.

Podcast: Inside Key Mining’s $303M Deal with Compass Digital Acquisition Corp. $CDAQF

We spoke with @keyminingcorp founders Cesar Lopez and John Ryan as well as Compass Digital Acquisition Corp. CEO Tom Hennessy to break down their $303M business combination.

Titanium, copper and water. What do they have in common? All will be products of one of the latest companies to head to the public markets via a SPAC transaction.

Cesar and John discuss how they brought together a signature titanium mining project in Chile with a water desalination project that is set to support it. They lay out why they are combining these two assets with a copper project in Arizona and how both stand to benefit from the critical metals incentives in the Inflation Reduction Act.

Tom explains how this company fits in his growing family of SPAC transactions and what the roadmap ahead looks like for it beyond close and the listing this deal brings.

Give it a listen.

text:
AlphaTarget is now more than two years old, and I’ve been reflecting on what we’ve learned.

We’ve beaten the S&P 500 by a wide margin. I’m proud of that but what matters even more to us is how we build on it from here.

The last two years have been an extraordinary period for AI and technology and they’ve taught us a great deal about both opportunity and risk.

We’ve now become much more deliberate about portfolio construction and risk management. We still want to own the companies with the potential to reshape industries and compound capital for years but we also recognise that growth stocks have become super volatile and periods of extreme optimism are inevitably followed by sharp resets.

That means more active portfolio management, taking gains when appropriate, genuine hedging when conditions warrant it and holding more cash when markets become excessively extended.

We refined our portfolio management and hedging strategy this spring, and June and July provided the first serious test.

During those two months, many AI stocks fell 40–60%. AlphaTarget’s portfolio declined roughly 20%.

It was still a testing period but the portfolio held up considerably better than it had during previous periods of market volatility.

We don’t view that as the end of the story, it’s the beginning of a better process.

Our objective for the next several years is straightforward:

Find exceptional companies early. Participate aggressively when the opportunity is greatest and manage the portfolio actively to reduce drawdowns when the market inevitably becomes volatile.

The opportunity created by AI and the technologies surrounding it remains enormous.

At the same time, the longer this bull market runs, the greater the risk that parts of the market become speculative (real risk of an AI bubble in the future). I believe navigating that environment - knowing when to be aggressive and when to protect capital - will be one of the defining investment challenges over the next 2-3 years.

And frankly, I think the next 2-3 years could be even more interesting than the last two.

To all our subscribers, thank you for being on this journey with us.

If you’re discovering AlphaTarget for the first time, our research service provides institutional-quality research on the most promising companies in the public markets, along with timely Trading Alerts so subscribers can follow our portfolio decisions as they happen. https://t.co/YKr5pL7G2c

$72K is the ultimate test.

$NVDA Pushed Into Its Upper Bollinger Envelope (UPE) on Friday, NEXT MOVE? ⚠️

• $NVDA pushed into its Upper Bollinger Envelope (UPE), reaching $234.76, before being sharply rejected and closing back near the $230.50 nominal level—an area where it has recently closed twice before. Now we have a triple top at this level.

• In recent history, $NVDA has corrected almost consistently after pushing into the UPE. The animated, no-audio video below shows each prior occurrence and how far price subsequently moved lower.

• The move to $234.76 was important from a harmonics perspective. Notably, this price also exceeded the mid-May Wave 5 top by only a few pennies—a potentially significant technical event and an ideal area for price rejection. The level is highlighted in the video below.

• From here, my expected downside target is the $215–$220 range, potentially reaching either the Bollinger basis or the calculated Wave 4 low marked by the thick orange line.

The video below illustrates the historical UPE reactions and the key levels currently in play.

Matthew Shane Perkins, 47, to serve 15 years in prison
for defrauding about 200 investors of nearly $89 million

Perkins operated Forged Oak LLC between August 2023 and November 2025, claiming to be a “brilliant trader who consistently beat the market and rarely suffered losing days

In November 2025, Perkins provided an altered statement representing that the funds held over $133 million, when the actual balance was less than $13 million

Officials say Perkins lost tens of millions of dollars in day trading. He also siphoned off millions of dollars to pay for personal expenses, including a down payment on a home, a cabin, luxury vehicles, an airplane and an $80,000 hunting trip in British Columbia.

US homebuyers are walking away from deals at the highest rate in years:

14.0% of home-purchase agreements that went under contract fell through in July, the highest rate since November 2023.

The national cancellation rate has held between 13.0% and 14.0% over the last 4 years, well above the lower rates typical of the seller's market from 2020 to 2022.

Atlanta posted the highest cancellation rate last month, at 19.8%, followed by Houston at 19.6%, San Antonio at 18.7%, and Las Vegas at 18.6%.

This comes as sellers outnumber buyers by ~51%, near the highest percentage on record, giving buyers more options and making them more willing to walk away over inspection issues, low appraisals, or rejected concessions.

At the same time, high home prices and elevated mortgage rates are leaving buyers with less financial room, making unexpected costs or concerns about taking on large monthly payments more likely to derail deals.

The housing market is under historic pressure.

The bull market is gaining momentum:

The 200-day moving average of the S&P 500 has now risen for 329 consecutive trading sessions, the 4th-strongest streak over the last 10 years.

This follows a previous 460-session run that briefly ended in April 2025 following "Liberation Day," bringing the combined streak to ~800 sessions, which would be the 3rd-longest since 1990.

For perspective, the longest such stretch lasted 1,448 days during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble.

Historically, when the 200-day moving average was rising, the S&P 500 returned +8.5% per year on average since 1999.

By comparison, when the 200-day moving average was falling, the S&P 500 returned just +0.1% per year on average.

History suggests the bullish trend is far from over.

15+ year Treasuries have returned -2% per year on average over the last 10 years, their worst performance in history.

This is also only the 2nd period in data going back to 1936 where Treasuries have posted negative 10-year annualized returns.

By comparison, US stocks have returned +15% per year on average, while commodities have returned +11% per year on average over the same timeframe.

To put this into perspective, before the 2020 pandemic, Treasuries gained +9% per year on average over a 10-year period.

Since the start of 2020, the popular bond-tracking ETF $TLT has dropped -26%, with its biggest drawdown at -34%.

The bond market is no longer the safe haven it once was.

Russian gold flows into Hong Kong are skyrocketing:

In the first 7 months of 2026, Hong Kong’s gold imports from Russia rose to $14.4 billion.

This is already +50% above the full-year figure of $9.6 billion recorded in 2025.

This is also nearly triple the amount seen in 2023 and 2024.

The surge reflects the redirection of Russian gold exports toward Asian markets after Western sanctions effectively closed London and other Western hubs to Russian bullion.

Hong Kong has no such restrictions, allowing it to increasingly serve as a major trading hub for Russian gold entering the Asian market.

The flow of Russian gold into Asia is accelerating.

text:
The de-dollarization trend appears to be far from global:

The US Dollar’s proportion of official global FX reserves is down to 57%, its lowest in at least 30 years.

This percentage has declined -20 points since 1999, with China and, to a lesser extent, Russia driving much of the decline.

Over the same period, the combined proportion of the 4 major reserve currencies, the US Dollar, Yen, Euro and Pound, has fallen -12 percentage points, to ~87%, also its lowest in at least 30 years.

Meanwhile, roughly equal numbers of countries increased and decreased their US Dollar reserves between 2015 and 2023.

Therefore, the decline is heavily concentrated among a small number of reserve holders, suggesting the US Dollar's position in most reserve portfolios remains relatively stable.

The threat to the US Dollar’s reserve currency status appears limited.

What is happening with the US job market?

US job openings for June were revised down by -177,000 vacancies, their largest monthly downward revision since November 2025.

This also marks the 3rd consecutive monthly downward revision.

Furthermore, the number of hires for June was revised down by -16,000, while the number of quits was revised lower by -19,000.

At the same time, the number of layoffs and discharges was revised up by +19,000.

As a result, job openings have now been revised down in 38 of the last 43 months.

US labor market data is becoming increasingly difficult to read with confidence.

The US AI infrastructure boom is making history.

There are now ~90 US data centers with more than 100 megawatts (MW) of power in operation, the highest count on record.

This figure is set to more than triple by 2030, to ~280, if all currently planned projects are completed.

Over the same period, tech companies are expected to spend ~$7.0 trillion on data centers.

Meanwhile, Amazon, $AMZN, Microsoft, $MSFT, Alphabet, $GOOGL, and Meta, $META, have already signed more than $1.5 trillion in data center leases since the AI boom began, including commitments that have yet to take effect.

The AI buildout is one of the largest capital spending cycles in history.

Foreign investors are piling into US assets:

Investors outside the US now hold a record ~$39 trillion in US equities, Treasuries, corporate, agency, and other bonds.

Since the 2022 bear market, this figure has surged +$16 trillion, or +70%.

Over this period, foreign holdings of US stocks have doubled to a record $24 trillion, accounting for ~62% of the total.

At the same time, foreign Treasury holdings have grown +$2 trillion, to $8 trillion, an all-time high, representing ~21% of the total.

To put this into perspective, during the 2020 pandemic, investors outside the US held just ~$19 trillion in US assets.

Foreign demand for US assets is historically strong.

Utilities stocks are at their most oversold levels in years:

Only ~25% of the S&P 500 utility sector stocks are now trading above their 200-day moving average, the lowest proportion since February 2024.

This marks a sharp reversal from ~90% recorded in July.

Utilities have gone from one of the market’s strongest groups, after gaining +11.5% through February, to one of its weakest, with the sector now up only +2.3% year-to-date, putting it on track for its worst year relative to the S&P 500 since 2023.

This comes as rising Treasury yields are making dividends from utility stocks less attractive while also raising borrowing costs for the capital-intensive sector.

The 10Y Treasury yield is now 1.84 percentage points higher than the dividend yield of S&P 500 utilities, near the widest spread since 2007, after peaking at 2.00 percentage points in July.

Investor demand for defensive stocks is fading.

There is an employment recession in the US Information sector.

The Information industry shed -23,000 jobs in August, bringing employment down to 2.75 million, its lowest since the 2020 pandemic.

The Information sector includes software publishing, data processing and computing infrastructure, web search, telecom, broadcasting, publishing, and other information services.

Excluding 2020, this is the lowest reading since April 2015.

Since the November 2022 peak, Information employment has contracted -270,000, or -12%.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis and its aftermath, employment in this industry also fell -12%, or -350,000 jobs.

AI is increasingly replacing skilled human labor across parts of the Information sector.

original.text:
Getting a lot of questions on my semiconductor call, mostly from fundamental guys pointing at revenue growth. Let me be clear where this call comes from, because most of you are arguing against a point I'm not making.

I agree with you on the fundamentals. I've written entire articles laying out the semi bull case. Revenue, AI infrastructure demand, all of it. Earnings are still climbing. Even through the recent selloff, chip earnings revisions were among the strongest in the entire market. None of that is in dispute.

That is not where my call comes from.

This is a technical call, and it has plenty of outs. My whole framework is price structure / trend, not the income statement. And the thing fundamental investors constantly underweight is that price and fundamentals disconnect all the time.  That's the entire reason markets exist. If price and fundamentals were always in sync there'd be nothing to trade and no edge to have. Price overshoots and undershoots the fundamentals in every single cycle.

So here's what the chart is telling me.

The $SOX more than doubled off its April 2025 low into the 2026 high. That is not a move you buy into late. And the recent break was violent. The index dropped 20% in under a month, its fastest correction since the dot com top in 2000. Over a trillion dollars came off the group in a matter of sessions. That doesn't happen in healthy early-stage trends. It happens in crowded ones.

Crowded is the key word. Semi concentration was sitting at record extremes into the highs. When everyone already owns it, there's no marginal buyer left to push it higher, just a stampede for the exit when it turns.

And you can already see the money moving. Software is putting up one of its sharpest rotations in years. Crypto names are catching a bid. Capital is leaving the chips and going into what lagged. That's what a leadership change looks like in real time.

So to be clear. I'm not cautious on semis because I think the business is bad. I think the business is great. I'm cautious on the chart because the move is extended, the trade is crowded, the correction was historic, and the rotation is already underway. Great business, stretched chart. Both can be true.

Fundamentals tell you what to own. The chart tells you when. I just see better risk reward elsewhere right now.

original.text:
Ethereum is for shipping.

Here are 35 things the Ethereum ecosystem launched, upgraded, and announced through August.

1/ GnosisDAO approved a vote to transition @gnosischain from its own L1 to a ZK-proven Ethereum L2 rollup with synchronous composability, so apps on Gnosis and Ethereum can interact in a single transaction.

2/ @BlackRock introduced the BlackRock Select Treasury Based Liquidity Fund (BSTBL) with a tokenized share class on Ethereum mainnet for managing stablecoin and digital asset reserves, and began tokenizing share classes of its $311B European money market fund series on Ethereum.

3/ @aztecnetwork launched Alpha v5, a protocol upgrade that reduced private transaction proving times and brought the first wave of privacy-preserving apps to the network.

4/ @Uniswap processed $1B+ in stock token volume and $20B+ in total volume on @RobinhoodCrypto's Robinhood Chain since its July launch.

5/ @ethPandaOps introduced the Platåberget testnet, preparing client implementations for Glamsterdam, Ethereum's next network upgrade.

6/ @Morpho crossed $880M in total deposits on Robinhood Chain in its first <2 months live and reached $5.75B in total deposits on @base.

7/ @web3privacy shared the Ethereum Privacy Ecosystem Mapping 2026, an updated map and repository covering Ethereum’s privacy ecosystem.

8/ @Revolut announced the phased rollout of its euro-denominated stablecoin EURR, live on Ethereum for eligible users.

9/ @aave v4 surpassed $525M in deposits on Ethereum.

10/ Coinbase Tokenized Stocks launched on @base for non-U.S. users, held 1:1 by a regulated custodian, owned in self-custody wallets, and usable across DeFi 24/7.

11/ @FreedomFactory opened presales for the PQ1, a fully open-source, air-gapped hardware wallet that signs with post-quantum cryptography through an Ethereum smart account.

12/ @OctantApp launched Epoch 13, its latest funding round, focused on privacy on Ethereum and across the open internet.

13/ @selfxyz and Google Cloud launched the USAT Mainnet Faucet on @Celo, letting anyone verified on Self claim USA₮.

14/ @PrivacyBoost launched the Privacy Boost App, a frontend to send private transfers from your connected wallet.

15/ @Whitechain_io, the distribution-focused network connected to the WhiteBit ecosystem, announced it is evolving from an L1 into an Ethereum L2 built on the OP Stack.

16/ @ether_fi added tokenized stocks, portfolio-backed loans through @aave, and other new features to its crypto neobank.

17/ @ethereuminsti announced its ecosystem funding round and supporter coalition, welcoming 100+ organizations to support Ethereum's institutional onboarding, and shared that Open Standard's Open USD stablecoin will launch on Ethereum on day one.

18/ @class_lambda and @gattacahq shared that their PropAMM (pAMMs) infrastructure has facilitated over $2B in total volume swapped on Ethereum.

19/ @theInterfold, an open-source protocol for confidential coordination and encrypted execution environments built on Ethereum, launched its Network Alpha production environment.

20/ @arbitrum activated ArbOS Elara, bringing more responsive fees and 4x bigger Stylus smart contracts to Arbitrum One, along with new features for chains built on the Arbitrum stack.

21/ @Uniswap launched v4 Permissioned Pools, a hook standard to enforce allowlists on swaps and liquidity deposits while the protocol itself stays permissionless, bringing regulated assets to AMM trading with launch partners @SuperstateInc, @Securitize, and Dowgo.

22/ @EthCoordinate, a new crypto-native organization building on the EthStaker community's work, was formed to support Ethereum governance coordination, facilitate stakeholder interaction, and accelerate Ethereum adoption.

23/ @MetaMask launched the MetaMask Agent Wallet, an agentic wallet with built-in spending limits, allowlists, and risk profiles.

24/ @ResearchHub, a tool for the open funding, publication, and discussion of scientific research built on Ethereum and @base, launched a new homepage to surface open research proposals and funding requests.

25/ @base opened applications for Base Batches 004, a startup accelerator program for 10 early-stage teams, and also launched Base Verify Onchain, a privacy-preserving identity layer for apps to enforce one-person-one-claim onchain distributions.

26/ @Cloudflare announced Wallets, enabling AI agents to buy APIs and content with stablecoin payments over the x402 payment standard.

27/ The @ethereumfndn launched the better[.]codes autoresearch challenge to advance post-quantum Ethereum, built with @zksecurityXYZ and @eigenlabs on @yukonresearch, putting a machine-verified security problem on a public leaderboard that anyone can push forward. @Lighter_xyz also launched the Lighter Prover challenge, an autoresearch competition to make Lighter's production exchange faster.

28/ Privacy-focused wallet @staycloakedxyz reached $650k in deposits and $1M in volume in its first 90 days live.

29/ @mtpelerin added support for @ensdomains names as sending and receiving addresses when creating personal IBANs for bank transfers in crypto.

30/ @Blockspace_ETH was announced, a company focused on out-of-protocol infrastructure for Ethereum blockspace.

31/ @0xprivacypools launched onchain payroll support, allowing employers to provide recurring wage payments with privacy for salary amounts and recipient addresses.

32/ Fake World Assets (FWA), a NFT gacha protocol by @token_works, launched the FWAir NFT distribution mechanism with an initial 111 item PFP collection.

33/ Builder @z0r0zzz launched zSwap, a fully onchain decentralized exchange built on Ethereum, with all code, including frontend and application logic, stored on mainnet smart contracts.

34/ MMO game @playcambria surpassed $10M in total game volume in August, and @LootSurvivor and Cambria launched a 72-hour onchain dungeon competition.

35/ @EFDevcon released the official Devcon 8 travel guide for Mumbai ahead of this year's Devcon 8 conference in November.

The average 401k balance is $167,970.

The median is $44,115.

4.6 million accounts, Vanguard's 2026 report.

Here's what the middle person has:

Under 25: $2,234
25 to 34: about $16,000
35 to 44: about $40,000
45 to 54: about $68,000
55 to 64: $84,700
65 and older: $103,202

That last one is the number.

$103,202 at a 4% withdrawal is $4,128 a year. $344 a month.

Fidelity says you should have 10x your salary saved by retirement. On a $60,000 income that's $600,000.

The median 65 year old has 17% of it…

28% of Vanguard 401k accounts hold less than $10,000.

And 25.8% of Gen X savers currently have a loan out against theirs. Highest of any generation.

So the typical American is retiring on $344 a month plus Social Security, and the average number everyone posts makes it look 4 times better than that.

Follow me with notifications on so you know when I make a new move in the market. This is very important.

If you don’t, you will regret it later. Your choice.

So they’re in Washington talking about their own tax rules, then a congressional household puts up to $12 million into them with dated calls, then they get added to the index.

Coincidence, obviously.

Right??

text:
Norway’s $2.3 TRILLION fund wants to cut $80 BILLION of US Treasuries.

They hold about $215 billion. The proposal takes Treasury exposure from 34.1% of the bond book down to 21.9%.

The reason isn’t political, at least not officially. Government bonds returned 0.5% in the first half of the year while the fund overall did 9.4%.

So they’re moving the money into corporate bonds and mortgage-backed securities instead. US non-government fixed income goes from 16.2% to 27.6%.

The biggest fund on earth is rotating out of Treasuries and into the thing that blew up in 2008, because Treasuries aren’t paying enough.

It’s a proposal though, not a decision. Norway’s Finance Ministry has to approve it, and they’ve said any changes happen gradually.

Net foreign private demand for Treasuries fell to $16.6 billion in June. The US 30 year is at 5.27%. Japan and the UK are both repricing.

Debt is going up and the buyers keep getting smaller…

text:
Last wk despite WTI +10% & ylds +2-7 bps across the curve, S&P/Nas/R2K +0.1%/+0.4%/+0.1%. $NVDA acquisition of Hugging Face & $Meta release of Muse Spark 1.3 last wk make both names more attractive into year-end.

My view is that LLMs increasingly bifurcate into 90%+ usage of open-source/ open-weight models in the future as companies optimize the right models for the right task. Since the focus on controlling AI expenditures, the Silicon Data token cost has fallen over 50% since late May but the weekly usage of tokens in models across OpenRouter has increased by 3.6x over this same time.

In addition, enterprises are increasingly focused on making sure their own proprietary data does not leak out when they use third party closed frontier LLMs.  Hugging Face is the premier central collaborative platform, repository, and toolkit for open-source and open-weight AI with over 18 million developers.

Nvidia has three customers that accounted for 44% of their revenues over the past six months and their largest customers are increasingly designing their own ASICs and in some cases selling them externally. A more diversified customer base that owns their own AI compute stack instead of renting from the big cloud service providers would help Nvidia with both of these issues. With this acquisition, Nvidia is in an even better position to sell enterprises a complete alternative AI stack (from the model to chips) where the customer will own their own data.

Valuation is also compelling. Nvidia trades at a 15x CY27 PE versus their own guidance for 70% revenue growth and the Big 3 public cloud service providers at 21-23x for 15-26% total revenue growth. The S&P trades at 19x for 9% revenue growth for comparison. Nvidia is also up “just”24% versus the Semiconductor Index up 66% following underperformance last year at up 39% versus 42%.

As for Meta, the stock is down 7% year-to-date after being up just 13% last year driven largely by concerns that 1) they can only monetize their near doubling in AI capex spend through efficiencies in their own business and 2) they were falling behind in the AI model race. The launch of the Muse Spark 1.3 API last week, catapulted Meta back to near frontier status (Top four in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index out of 10 models) but with aggressive token pricing (Bottom four in Cost per Task.) Open-weight versions of the Muse Spark lineup are coming soon. This will give the company another way to monetize their aggressive capex plans. 

This follows Meta's settlement in late August with state AGs on their youth addiction trial which was another overhang on the stock. Trading at 16x CY27 PE for 20% revenue growth is compelling with the settlement and Spark 1.3 launch as catalysts.

From a broader market perspective, I recommend caution between now and the US mid-terms for reasons I have fleshed out in prior posts including:
1) Don’t Fight the Fed given I believe a 9/16 hike is likely 2) September -0.5% on avg & up only 48% of the time
3) S&P drawdowns of 10% in lead-up to mid-terms
4) Bipartisan pushback against datacenter expansion
5) Iran dragging out hostilities through US mid-terms

Hi Larry, I should have probably made the post longer (despite the complaints I get) to flesh out my thoughts.  What I was trying to say is this will at least put some short-term downward pressure on the rise in yields vs if the Fed did nothing yet again.  

I structurally believe though that longer-term yields across have upward pressure until deficits start to come down which there seems no political will to do given the expansion in social programs and defense spending across the globe which seems structural in nature to name just two. In the US in particular, controlling the deficit is something neither political party seems to be that concerned with. 6% deficits is the highest ever outside a major war and debt crossing $40 trillion vs GDP at $33 trillion could be the straw that broke the camels back.  In addition, Japanese investors having yields near 3% for their own 10 year which is the highest levels since 1996 gives them more of a reason to sell some portion of their $1 trillion in US treasuries to buy JGBs. The UK at 5.1% for their 10y which at one point hit the highest levels at 5.3% since 2007 and is the second largest holder of US treasuries at $0.9 trillion is another problem. I think this ultimately ends poorly but who know how long the can gets kicked down the road before the bond market truly rebels.

text:
August NFP 162k vs 55K expected & 2m revision of +55K. IMO, odds favor Fed hike on 9/16 as a result. Even if CPI on 9/11 lower than expectations, inflation has been above 2% target for 65 months. Hike could also help cap rising 10/30y ylds which is long-term more important.

To me, it is hard to argue that 2% inflation is in fact is a hard target when it has not been there in over 5 years and the last six rate changes have been to cut rates starting 2 years ago. A rate hike is likely to help the Fed’s credibility going forward.

Finally, I doubt the Fed wants to risk having to raise rates on 10/28 given US mid-terms are only a few days later on 11/3. Given the political pressure on Fed independence, risking the need to do a rate hike that close to the election is probably something they would like to avoid given the likely political backlash.

text:
Last wk, SPX/Nas/R2K +0.5%/+0.8%/-1.5% w/ oil -4%. But a hawkish Warsh on Friday led to a bear flattening of the yield curve. Despite $NVDA guide of 70% CY27 rev growth vs consensus of 47%, SOX Index -2.3% while software $IGV +5.9% on solid earnings.

In general, many AI investors have been bullish on semiconductors and bearish on software on the belief that AI will displace many point solution software companies. This is why the SOX index is up 62% YTD and IGV is still only up 4% YTD versus the S&P +13%. Situational Awareness was the poster child for this type of positioning.

But since the unwinding of the Momentum trade which started on 6/22 (I wrote about these concerns on 6/20), IGV has rallied 25% while the SOX Index has declined 22% through 8/28. For perspective, the Morgan Stanley Momentum index (momentum long performance minus momentum short performance) from 6/22-8/28 is down 36% while their more concentrated TMT index is down 54%. But a bullish twist on AI for the software sector introduced recently is that AI agents will access software tools ~10-100x more often than humans.

On 8/6, $TEAM, which was in the bucket of software names widely considered at risk of being replaced by AI, rallied 35% the next day in reaction to solid earnings & outlook.

Then on 8/13, $WDAY rallied 18% on the news that private equity firm Silverlake might be pursuing an acquisition which I wrote probably put a floor underneath software. Workday was also supposed to be in the AI crosshairs and private equity has higher bars to clear given their use of leverage and holding period than a typical investor.

Then on 8/26, $CRM reported solid results, guidance and a deal with Anthropic (in which they also first invested in May of 2023.) The stock was up 23% in reaction the next day. This seemed to be a strong counterpoint to the SaaS-pocalypse worries. This strategic alliance allows users to execute actions natively inside Claude without needing to open traditional software screens. Salesforce also seems to be changing how they charge customers with fees more related to customer use and benefits to their business.

Then on 8/27, Workday reported results which were good enough but arguably acquisition prospects drove more of the stock reaction of +6% the next day from the slightly down opening price.

Historically, system of record, security and gaming software have been the only three areas I have liked within software. I now  wonder whether the fundamental implications of Atlassian, Workday and Salesforce are supportive of the technical reactions in the software stocks as a group as agentic AI continues to ramp.

So how do I square this with my concerns that the rapidly escalating amounts spent on AI by corporations has to come from somewhere? Annualized revenue run-rates for Anthropic and OpenAI have ramped from $29B to start the year to $105B just 7 months later. Software spending globally excluding AI was roughly $1 trillion in 2025. But IT services at $1.7 trillion is a bigger category which I believe still has risk. And finally, knowledge worker compensation is an even bigger category where disruption would be even less noticeable at an estimated $35-50 trillion in 2025 or roughly 30% of the global workforce. 

Looking forward, the deal on Friday for Venezuelan oil fields that hold the largest crude reserves in the world at 17-18% should get us off to a positive start to the week with declining oil prices. But a bit further out: 1) “Don’t Fight the Fed” given I believe a hike is likely on 9/16 because the 10/28 mtg is right before mid-terms, 2) September has the poorest  seasonality of all months, 3) there is even worse seasonality than normal during mid-term election years (see prior posts for more detail) and 4) recent bipartisan pushback against datacenter expansion (one of the few things both sides seem to agree on though I believe this is wrong and hope it will change with more education) puts pressure on the AI infrastructure names.

As Warren Buffett says, the market has to keep pitching but you do not need to swing.

Here is your $CSCO comparison. Cisco was forecasting sustainable revenue growth of 30-50% in 2000. This is an excerpt from their earning release on May 8th 2001: "The first four months of 2001 were extremely challenging as we went from year-over-year bookings in excess of 70% in November, to 30% negative growth within a span of several months. This may be the fastest deceleration any company of our size has ever experienced," said John Chambers, president and CEO of Cisco Systems. 

To be clear, I am not saying this is where we are today on a fundamental basis on the AI trade.  I think this is a problem sometime in 2027 at the earliest. But my point is to not rely on backlog or bookings that can change very rapidly especially when you have large customer concentration. $NVDA had two customers last quarter than combined were 39% of revenues.

text: When the Vix Index is at an extreme, in either direction, that is when I get concerned of a move in the S&P in the opposite direction of whatever it has been doing recently. Having said that, with the Vix Index closing at 14.41 today, very close to its YTD low of 14.25, and the risks I see going into the mid-terms in early November, this is more an indication of complacency to me making the market more susceptible to a sudden shock. Having said that, the good thing is it makes option based hedging much cheaper due to the low vol.
